title: Real Abraha campaigns, but the elephant story stays contested

points.label: A memory of Abraha
points.text: **Pregill** hesitates to call it mere trope “given the mounting inscriptional evidence”. **Robin** finds a failed expedition plausible; a damaged Yemeni text naming Abraha, published 2025, may read “elephants”, hypothetically.

points.label: A legend retold
points.text: **De Prémare** sees a Qur’anic midrash on Ptolemy’s elephants in **3 Maccabees 2–6**, turned by angels on his own soldiers. **Dye** finds this very plausible and the Abraha link “absurd”. **Beck** also reads Maccabees, arguing African war elephants were long gone.

points.label: The birth-year problem
points.text: If the campaign was the one inscribed in **552**, it falls decades before Muhammad’s probable birth. **Kropp** calls the shared year a hagiographical construct; **Cuypers** reads it symbolically.
points.who: Kropp; Cuypers, in the Qur’an Seminar

bottom_text: Still divided, says Pregill. Inscriptions prove Abraha’s central Arabian campaigns, but the 552 text never names Mecca, while the legend reading must explain why tradition swapped stories (Khalfallah).
source_label: Qur’an Seminar Commentary on Q 105 · al-Bāriqī & Robin (2025)
